_comment: The renderer registry. Adding a video model to this pipeline should be a
DATA change, not a code change — which is the whole reason this file exists.
Every field here was a hardcoded constant inside plan.py until 2026-08-15.
That was fine while H3 was the only renderer and wrong the moment a shot
needed something H3 cannot do (be driven by existing audio). A second model
does not share H3's frame grid, its fps, its canvas ceiling or its cost.
`provides` is the vocabulary the router matches shots against:
both_ends      conditions on a first AND last keyframe (bounded drift)
first_frame    conditions on a starting image only
native_audio   invents its own audio from the text prompt (dialogue, SFX)
audio_driven   takes EXISTING audio as the driver — lips, head, body
silent         can be asked to produce no audio
`status` is load-bearing: `measured` means someone ran it on this hardware
and wrote the number down. `unverified` means it came from a README. Never
promote a number without an experiment - see the 124-frame ceiling that

h3.label: MiniMax H3 (local, gpu-worker)
notes: 0.94MP is the hard OOM ceiling for single-ended; both-ends wants less.
Cannot be driven by existing audio - it only ever makes its own.

infinitetalk.label: InfiniteTalk on Wan 2.1-I2V-14B (local, PROPOSED)
notes: This is what Maestro uses, and the reason its music videos sync.
Audio drives lips, head, posture and expression together, rather than
patching a mouth onto finished footage.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS FROM DOCUMENTATION, NOT FROM OUR CARD. Full
pipeline is reported at 18-22GB peak; Q4 GGUF is the 12-16GB route and
is described as a quality/speed compromise. Apache 2.0.
Chunks for unlimited length, so max_frames is per chunk, not per shot.
Do not route real work here until status is `measured`.
